notes: Evals set up local artifact files via the `files` field; the subagent runs with cwd at that checkout. PRD-issue and ticket detection go through `gh issue list`, which returns nothing in a sandbox without a GitHub remote — that is fine: assertions only require the scan to attempt the gh lookup and to report GitHub-backed stages as unknown/unsatisfied when gh yields nothing. The behaviour spec is: (1) the skill triggers on 'where do I start / what product docs exist' prompts, (2) it reports which of the six lifecycle stages (ideate -> approach -> roadmap -> PRD -> plan -> tickets) are satisfied, and (3) it recommends a single entry point / next skill.

evals.name: empty-repo-start
evals.prompt: just cloned this and I want to add a product feature — where should I start? do any product docs or plans already exist?
evals.expected_output: A short scan report showing none of the six lifecycle artifacts are present, so no stages are satisfied, with a recommended entry point of the ideate skill (or chat-to-approach if the user already has a conversation to capture).

assertions.text: The scan checks for all six artifacts: ideate report (./ideas/reports/*-ideate.md), approach doc (./docs/approach.md), roadmap (./roadmap.html), PRD issue (gh issue titled [PRD]), plan file (./plans/*.md), and tickets (non-PRD gh issues)
The report states that no lifecycle stages are satisfied (or explicitly lists each of the six stages as not satisfied)
The report recommends a single entry point, and it is the ideate skill (or chat-to-approach) since the earliest stage is unsatisfied
The report does not fabricate artifacts that were not found on disk or via gh

evals.name: ideate-only
evals.prompt: what's the state of the product docs here and what should I do next?
evals.expected_output: Report shows the ideate stage satisfied (an ideate report exists) and every later stage unsatisfied, with a recommended next step of chat-to-approach to produce the approach doc.

files.content:
# Ideate report

Recommended next idea: a diff-based freshness score.

assertions.text: The report marks the ideate stage as satisfied and cites ./ideas/reports/2026-05-01-ideate.md as the evidence
The report marks the approach, roadmap, PRD, plan, and tickets stages as not satisfied
The recommended entry point is the first unsatisfied stage — the approach stage — and names the chat-to-approach skill as the next step

evals.name: approach-and-roadmap
evals.prompt: where are we in the product pipeline for this repo? point me at the next skill to run.
evals.expected_output: Report shows approach and roadmap stages satisfied (approach.md and roadmap.html exist), recommends to-prd since the PRD stage is the earliest gap.

files.content:
# Approach

_Last updated 2026-05-02_

## Problem

Users can't tell what to build next.

assertions.text: The report marks the approach stage satisfied (./docs/approach.md) and the roadmap stage satisfied (./roadmap.html)
The report marks the PRD, plan, and tickets stages as not satisfied
The scan attempts a GitHub lookup (gh issue list) to check for a [PRD] issue and for tickets
The recommended entry point is the PRD stage, naming the to-prd skill as the next step

evals.name: plan-ready-tickets-next
evals.prompt: I think most of the planning is done — what's left before I start coding?
evals.expected_output: Report shows ideate, approach, roadmap, and plan artifacts present locally; recommends breaking the plan into tickets via to-tickets as the entry point, since tickets are the remaining gap.

files.content:

assertions.text: The report marks the ideate, approach, roadmap, and plan stages as satisfied and cites the corresponding files (including ./plans/feature-x.md for the plan stage)
The scan attempts a gh issue list lookup to determine whether a [PRD] issue exists and whether tickets already exist
The report identifies tickets as the remaining unsatisfied stage and recommends to-tickets as the entry point
The report presents the six stages in lifecycle order: ideate -> approach -> roadmap -> PRD -> plan -> tickets
